A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the random matrices with heavy-tailed entries are almost as good as the random matrices with sub-gaussian entries.
the set of singular values of random matrices with i.i. d. heavy-tailed random entries is well approximated by the set of singular value of random matrices with sub-gaussian entries.
the set of singular values of a random matrix with i. i. d. entries is a “typical” set of size exp(δn).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of the entries of A plays a minor role in the analysis, as long as they have finite second moments.
the random matrix A is well-approximated by a finite number of ellipsoids.
for random matrices with heavy-tailed entries the smallest singular value is not significantly larger than the one of random matrices with sub-gaussian entries.
